messages.author: 2b2a7dccb793ae6c
messages.subject: parameter range
parts:
Dear Stan Users,
When I specify a parameter, I found that <lower=0, upper=1> means [0,1]. What if I want (0,1) instead? Otherwise I got lots of warnings of "Shape parameter is 0, but must be > 0!"

Thanks!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] parameter range
parts:
All the bounds are inclusive.

Although you might be tempted to do something like `lower = 0.0001`, please don't. If you're getting a lot of draws on the boundary, there's something going on with the model and you should take a look. Perhaps the data is pushing the parameter up at that boundary. If so, you might want to rethink the statistical model. If it's underflow or overflow somewhere else, then you should take care of the numerical issues.

It's hard to help without seeing the actual program, so those are all guesses.


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] parameter range
parts:
The only way to get a parameter value of 0 or 1 is
to overflow or underflow on the unconstrained scale.
Stan samples on (-inf, inf), but then maps back to
(0, 1) using inv_logit. inv_logit will overflow or
underflow if the unconstrained value is too large or
too small (outside of (-1000, 1000) or so).

The problem comes from the Hamiltonian integrator not being able
to follow really sharp curvature using only gradient information.
So we take a step along the gradient and wind up overflowing or
underflowing.

If the model's OK and it's just a numerical problem with extreme
steps, you can mitigate the issue by reducing stepsize and
increasing adapt_delta (latter is target acceptance rate).

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] parameter range
parts:
On Wednesday, July 13, 2016 at 12:27:15 PM UTC-4, Jingjing Chen wrote:
I thought that step size is optimized during the warm-up process. Is that true?
If I want to manually specify the acceptance rate, what script should I write in PyStan?

Specifying a stepsize corresponds to setting an initial stepsize, and doesn't prevent it from learning the stepsize during the warmup period. For specifying the target acceptance rate you want to use adapt_delta, which in PyStan can be set using the control argument, which is a dictionary of parameters that affect the sampler: http://pystan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html

Jonah
